path_decisions.rationale: Discovered critical SHORT-direction bug in profit_target_exit() -- function only checks close >= entry_price*(1+pct), which never triggers for SHORT positions where close must fall below entry. This is the #1 bottleneck reducing win rate for mean_reversion and funding_rate strategies.

Found config/code default mismatches across all strategies -- YAML configs define different profit_take_pct values than code defaults, and backtests likely run against code defaults, producing misleading optimization results.

RSI-adaptive profit targets are only implemented in trend_following; mean_reversion, volatility_breakout, momentum_rotation, funding_rate, and elliott_wave all lack adaptive targets despite RSI being computed in mean_reversion. This is a direct win rate limiter for the mean-reversion family.

Multiple missing mechanisms compound: (1) no trailing stop in mean_reversion on_bar path, (2) no stop_loss at all in profit_target_exit, (3) event-driven path completely missing profit_target_exit and max_holding_bars, (4) signal_quality_metrics uses next-bar return as win rate proxy but actual strategy win rate depends on full trade lifecycle.

candidate_solution.summary: 5 critical bottlenecks limiting win rate to <65%, with code evidence and specific fixes

bottlenecks.title: profit_target_exit() broken for SHORT positions
bottlenecks.evidence: target_price = entry_price * (1.0 + profit_take_pct) and close >= target_price -- this logic ONLY checks if price went UP. For SHORT entries, profit occurs when price goes DOWN. The function needs direction awareness: for SHORT, target = entry_price * (1 - pct) and check close <= target.
bottlenecks.impact: All SHORT-side trades from mean_reversion, volatility_breakout, funding_rate, momentum_rotation strategies NEVER hit profit target, relying solely on time-based max_holding_bars exit or other exit signals. This directly reduces win rate by forcing profitable SHORT trades into arbitrary time-based exits.
bottlenecks.fix: Add direction parameter to profit_target_exit(); use entry_direction to select target_price = entry_price * (1 + pct) for LONG and entry_price * (1 - pct) for SHORT

bottlenecks.title: Event-driven on_bar path missing profit_target_exit and max_holding_bars for mean_reversion
bottlenecks.evidence: on_bar() calls _latest_signal() which returns (entry_direction, exit_bool). The exit_bool at line 107-109 only checks bb_upper/bb_lower x 0.98 + exit_rsi conditions. No profit_target_exit or max_holding_bars check exists. Only generate_signals() at line 146 applies profit_target_exit.
bottlenecks.impact: In live/paper trading (event-driven mode), mean_reversion positions can be held indefinitely if price never reaches the opposite band. This causes both: (a) winning trades that revert slowly lose their gains to eventual adverse moves, and (b) losing trades held too long amplify losses.
bottlenecks.fix: Add position tracking state to MeanReversionStrategy (entry_price, bars_since_entry) and check profit_target/max_holding in on_bar()

bottlenecks.title: Config YAML vs code default parameter mismatches
bottlenecks.evidence: mean_reversion YAML: take_profit_pct=0.05, trailing_stop_pct=0.02 -- but code default profit_take_pct=0.03 and no trailing_stop_pct param. trend_following YAML: take_profit_pct=0.15 -- code default=0.10. volatility_breakout YAML: take_profit_pct=0.10, trailing_stop_atr_multiplier=2.0 -- code default profit_take_pct=0.05, trailing_stop_atr_mult=2.5. The YAML keys (take_profit_pct, stop_loss_pct) don't match code param names (profit_take_pct).
bottlenecks.impact: Backtests may use code defaults while traders think YAML is active. The key name mismatch (take_profit_pct vs profit_take_pct) means YAML config may never be read into strategy params, making all 'configured' values dead letters.
bottlenecks.fix: Unify YAML param keys with code param names; add config loading bridge in strategy __init__ that reads YAML values into _params

bottlenecks.title: RSI-adaptive profit targets missing from mean_reversion, volatility_breakout, and other strategies
bottlenecks.evidence: Only trend_following.py implements RSI-adaptive profit targets (lines 257-267): when RSI>70 at entry, tighten target to 80%; when RSI<30, loosen to 120%. mean_reversion.py computes RSI at line 127 but never uses it for adaptive exit sizing. volatility_breakout has no RSI-adaptive logic either.
bottlenecks.impact: For mean_reversion specifically, entries near RSI 30 (oversold) suggest stronger reversion potential -> should use wider profit targets. Entries near RSI 50 (weak signal) should use tighter targets. Without adaptation, the fixed 3% target either cuts winners short or lets mean-reverted trades reverse.
bottlenecks.fix: Add rsi_adaptive_profit boolean param to mean_reversion.py, implementing same logic as trend_following: oversold entries get 1.2x target, overbought entries get 0.8x target

bottlenecks.title: No stop_loss mechanism in profit_target_exit -- only profit_target + max_holding
bottlenecks.evidence: profit_target_exit() has only two exit conditions: (1) close >= target_price (profit), (2) bars_since_entry >= max_holding_bars (time). There is no stop_loss_pct parameter or downside exit. The triple_barrier_labels() in barriers.py does implement all three barriers but is only used for validation labeling, not live exit logic.
bottlenecks.impact: Without stop_loss, adverse trades held until max_holding_bars accumulate full loss. For mean_reversion with max_holding_bars=10 on 4h bars, that is 40 hours of drawdown with no protection. This disproportionately hurts win rate because a single large loss wipes out many small wins.
bottlenecks.fix: Add stop_loss_pct parameter to profit_target_exit() and check close <= entry_price * (1 - stop_loss_pct) for LONG / close >= entry_price * (1 + stop_loss_pct) for SHORT

interaction_effects.issue: In trend_following.py:292-294, trailing_exits is computed AFTER profit_exits. But the in_pos tracking loop at lines 282-291 resets in_pos=False on EITHER exits OR profit_exits. This means trailing_exits can trigger on the same bar as profit_target_exit, creating a double-exit that is benign for backtesting but could cause issues in live trading (two FLAT signals emitted).

mean_reversion.py:97-105 uses vol_ok as one of 3 conditions counted toward min_conditions=2. But the volume_threshold code default is 0.8 while YAML sets it to 1.2. At 0.8, volume confirmation is nearly always satisfied (80% of volume MA), making it a near-free condition. At 1.2, it filters meaningfully. This means code-default backtests over-count vol_ok as a confirming condition, inflating entry count with weak signals.

missing_mechanisms: No trailing stop in mean_reversion at all (YAML defines trailing_stop_pct:0.02 but code doesn't use it)
No partial profit taking (common in top quant systems: close 50% at 1R, let rest run)
No dynamic ATR-based position sizing in profit_target (use ATR to set target distance)

estimated_win_rate_impact.B1: SHORT bug: -5 to -8% win rate (all SHORT trades lose profit target exit)
estimated_win_rate_impact.B2: Event-driven gap: -3 to -5% in live mode (positions held too long)
estimated_win_rate_impact.B3: Config mismatch: -2 to -4% (suboptimal params used vs intended)
estimated_win_rate_impact.B4: No RSI-adaptive: -2 to -3% (fixed targets cut winners or let losers run)
estimated_win_rate_impact.B5: No stop_loss: -3 to -5% (large losses disproportionate impact on win rate)

evidence_anchors.note: Only works for LONG direction; SHORT positions never reach this target

evidence_anchors.quote: exit_ = (close > bb_upper * 0.98 and rsi > self._exit_rsi_overbought) or (close < bb_lower * 0.98 and rsi < self._exit_rsi_oversold)
evidence_anchors.note: Event-driven exit logic has no profit_target or max_holding check
generate_signals uses profit_target_exit but on_bar does not -- backtest/live inconsistency
YAML uses take_profit_pct (0.05) but code uses profit_take_pct (0.03); trailing_stop_pct defined but never read
RSI-adaptive targets implemented only in trend_following, missing from all other strategies

notes: The SHORT-direction bug in profit_target_exit (B1) is likely the single largest win rate bottleneck. Combined with the event-driven path gap (B2), mean_reversion SHORT trades in live mode have almost no profitable exit mechanism beyond the bb_lower*0.98 RSI exit, which only triggers when price returns near the band -- effectively a mean-reversion wait rather than a profit capture. The config/code mismatch (B3) means all backtesting to date may have used suboptimal defaults.
